   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$.

   204	                  drawn from the line-point distribution (see

   211			\item \label{enu:qld-comm-cons} (\textbf{Commutation consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_{a}$, where the answer summation is over $a\in \F_2$.

Then 
   214			\[
   215				\E_{\omega \, : \, \tr((r_\xpt \cdot
   216	                          u_\xpt) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot u_\zpt)) \neq 0} \Lambda_\omega = 1 - O(\eps)\;.
   217			\]
   218	
   219		\item \label{enu:qld-ms-cons} (\textbf{Magic square consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over anticommuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$,
   220		\begin{gather}
   221			M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_{a} \;,\\
   222			M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}_{a}\;,

   231		Since the question types are sampled according to the type graph $G^\Pauli$ of
   232	  finite size in \cref{fig:type-graph-pauli} in the game
   233	  $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$, the probability of any of the subtests of
   234	  $\decider^\pauli_\qldparams$ (described in \cref{fig:decider_pauli})

   237	  \ref{enu:qld-cons},~\ref{enu:qld-ld},~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} of the
   238	  lemma follow directly from the corresponding tests in
   239	  \cref{fig:decider_pauli} (where \Cref{enu:qld-ld} follows from the

   244	  For the remaining items, recall that by Fact~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   245	  the probability that a tuple $\omega=(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled as
   246	  question content for a question of type $\Pair$, $(\Pair,W)$, $\Constraint_i$
   247	  or $\Variable_j$ is commuting is at least $(1 - 3md/q) \cdot (1/2)$, which is
   248	  at least $1/4$ assuming $6md \leq q$. We claim this assumption holds
   249	  without loss of generality. Indeed, observe that the function
   250	  $\delta$ in \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix} is monotonically increasing in $a$, so without loss of generality we may assume that $a
   251	  \geq 6$.  Then it follows that we may assume that $6md \leq q$
   252	  without loss of generality, since otherwise, $\delta \geq a md /q
   253	  \geq 1$ and the conclusion of the theorem holds trivially.
   254	  The same lower bound holds for the probability that $\omega$ is anticommuting.

   271			\begin{equation}

   274			\end{equation}
   275			\item On average over uniformly random $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, 
   276			\begin{align}
   277				X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)
   278	                        Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob\notag\\
   279													&       \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (-1)^{\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
   280	                          \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))} \, Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) \otimes \Id_\bob	\;.	\label{eq:pts-obs-commutation}

   286	We first establish~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-consistency}. Fix a $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$. From item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} and the data processing inequality (Fact~\ref{fact:data-processing}), using that the question type $(\Point,W)$ has constant probability of being sampled by $\sampler^\pauli$, we get that on average over $u \in \F_q$,

   288		M^{(\Point,W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot r) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot r) = a]}\;,
   289	\]
   290	where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$. Equation~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-consistency} follows directly from~\Cref{lem:povm-to-obs}. 
   291	
   292	We now establish~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}. We have that on average over {commuting} $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ each of the approximate consistency relations hold, for any $W\in\{X,Z\}$:
   293	\begin{align*}
   294		&& M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W)=a]} \otimes \Id_\bob &\simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_a && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications})}\\
   295		&& &\simeq_\eps M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-comm})} \\
   296		&& &\simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}\;. && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} and Fact~\ref{fact:data-processing})}
   297	\end{align*}
   298	Fact~\ref{fact:agreement} then implies that on average over commuting $\omega$, 
   299	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-11}
   300		M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W)=a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}\;.
   301	\end{equation}
   302	Since
   303	$\{M^{\Pair,\omega}_{\beta_X,\beta_Z} \}$ is projective,
   304	\Cref{eq:lc-11} puts us in
   305	a position to apply Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}, setting
   306	$A^{x}_{a,b} = M^{(\Point, X), u_X}_{[\tr(\cdot r_X) = b]}$,
   307	$C^{x}_{a,c} = M^{(\Point, Z), u_Z}_{[\tr(\cdot r_Z) = c]}$, and
   308	$B^{x}_{a,b,c} = M^{\Pair, \omega}_{b,c}$. It follows that
   309	\begin{equation}
   310	\label{eq:qld-obs-comm}
   311		 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=b]} M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=c]} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps  M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=c]} M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=b]}  \otimes \Id_\bob
   312	\end{equation}
   313	on average over commuting $\omega$. Then for every $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, since the measurements $\{M^{\tvar,x}_a\}$ are projective we get that
   314	\begin{align}
   315		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) &= \Big ( \Id - 2 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} \Big ) \Big ( \Id - 2 M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]}  \Big ) \notag\\
   316		&= I - 2 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} - 2 M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]} + 4 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]}\;.\label{eq:lc-12}
   317	\end{align}
   318	Applying~\eqref{eq:qld-obs-comm} with $b = c = 1$ to commute the
   319	measurement operators in the the fourth term
   320	in~\eqref{eq:lc-12}, and performing the same steps in reverse, we deduce that on average over commuting $\omega$,
   321	\[
   322		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \approx_\eps  Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt).
   323	\]
   324	This shows the ``commuting'' part of~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}.
   325	
   326	Now we consider the case that $\omega$ is anticommuting. Item~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}, combined with \Cref{lem:povm-to-obs}, implies that the following two approximations hold on average over anticommuting $\omega$:
   327	\begin{gather}
   328		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} \;,\label{eq:lc-11a}\\
   329		Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}\;,\label{eq:lc-11b}
   330	\end{gather}
   331	where for $j\in\{1,5\}$, $M^{\Variable_j,\omega} = M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_0-M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_1$.
   332	
   333	For all anticommuting $\omega$, let $\eps_\omega = 1 -
   334	\Lambda_\omega$, where $\Lambda_\omega$ is defined in
   335	item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}. From
   336	item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} we get
   337	that $\E_{\omega \text{ anticomm.}} \eps_\omega \leq
   338	O(\eps)$. For each anticommuting $\omega$,
   339	Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity} implies that
   340	\[ \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   341	  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   342	  M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;. \]
   343	Thus, averaging over anticommuting $\omega$, and applying Jensen's
   344	inequality to the definition of $\approx_{\eps}$, we obtain the same
   345	anticommutation relation with error $ \E_{\omega \text{anticomm.}}
   346	\eps_{\omega}^{1/2} \leq (\E_{\omega \text{anticomm.}}
   347	\eps_\omega)^{1/2} = O(\eps^{1/2})$. In summary, on average over anticommuting $\omega$, 
   348	\begin{equation}
   349	\label{eq:qld-implication-ms-anticomm}
   350	\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} -\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;.
   351	\end{equation}
   352	Using \ref{fact:add-a-proj} twice we get from~\eqref{eq:lc-11a} and~\eqref{eq:lc-11b} that on average over anticommuting $\omega$,
   353	\begin{gather}
   354		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega}  M^{\Variable_5,\omega}\;, \\
   355		Z^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) X^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}  M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;.
   356	\end{gather}
   357	Using~\eqref{eq:qld-implication-ms-anticomm} we get that on average over anticommuting $\omega$, we have
   358	\[
   359	X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt)X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)  \otimes \Id_\bob\;.
   360	\]
   361	This shows the ``anticommuting'' part of~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}.
   362	\end{proof}

   415	\paragraph{The strategy under analysis.}
   416	For the remainder of this chapter, as well as in
   417	Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, we fix
   418	an admissible parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   419	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}) and a strategy
   420	$\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ for the game
   421	$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability
   422	at least $1 - \eps$, for some $\eps \geq 0$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   423	bipartite state on registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ with associated
   424	Hilbert spaces $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$. The symbol
   425	$M$ denotes the measurement operators of both players; which player is
   426	meant is indicated by the register on which the operator acts (for
   427	example, $M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}$ indicates that
   428	$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ is viewed as an operator acting on register

   431	The analysis requires the measurements of $\mathcal{S}$ to be projective;
   432	the following lemma shows that this may be assumed without loss of
   433	generality.
   434	
   435	\begin{lemma}[Reduction to a projective strategy]
   436		\label{lem:projective-strategy-setup}

   438		\leanok
   439		\uses{def:admissible, def:pauli-question-distribution, def:pauli-win-predicate, def:tensor-product-strategy, def:tensor-product-value, def:projective-strategy-general}
   440		Let $(q,m,d)$ be an admissible parameter tuple
   441		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}) and let
   442		$\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ be a strategy for the game
   443		$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   444		bipartite state on registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$. Then there
   445		exists a projective strategy
   446		(Definition~\ref{def:projective-strategy-general}) for
   447		$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ whose success probability
   448		equals that of $\mathcal{S}$ and whose state is the extension
   449		\[
   450			(\ket{\psi} \ot \ket{0\cdots 0} \ot \ket{0\cdots 0})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}

   455	\begin{proof}
   456		\uses{thm:naimark, def:tensor-product-value, def:tensor-product-strategy}
   457		Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}), applied with the
   458		families of all of the first player's measurements on register
   459		$\mathsf{A}$ and all of the second player's on register $\mathsf{B}$,
   460		yields an auxiliary space and a projective sub-measurement replacing
   461		each family on each register, together with a product auxiliary state,
   462		such that every correlation
   463		$\bra{\psi} M^{x}_a \ot M^{y}_b \ket{\psi}$ of $\mathcal{S}$ is
   464		reproduced on the extended state. Each auxiliary space embeds into a
   465		register of finitely many qubits; extend each dilated sub-measurement
   466		to the enlarged register by adding to one fixed outcome both the
   467		projector onto the orthogonal complement of the embedded subspace and
   468		the residual projector of the sub-measurement. The outcome operators
   469		remain mutually orthogonal projectors, now summing to the identity,
   470		and no correlation changes: the complement projector annihilates the
   471		extended state, which is supported in the embedded subspace, and so
   472		does each residual projector, because for each question pair the
   473		reproduced correlations sum to one --- the original families being
   474		POVMs (Definition~\ref{def:tensor-product-strategy}) --- which forces
   475		the projector $\Id$ minus the sum of each dilated sub-measurement to
   476		have zero mass on the extended state. Finally, since the auxiliary
   477		state is a product state, a unitary acting on each player's ancilla
   478		qubits alone carries it to $\ket{0 \cdots 0} \ot \ket{0 \cdots 0}$;
   479		conjugating the projective measurements by the same unitaries
   480		preserves projectivity and all correlations. The success probability
   481		of a strategy is a linear combination of its correlations, weighted by
   482		the question distribution and the win predicate
   483		(Definition~\ref{def:tensor-product-value}), and is therefore
   484		unchanged.

    51	\begin{definition}
    52	Given integer $d,m$ and a prime power $q$ we denote by $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables
    53	  with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When the field is clear from context we write $\ideg_{d,m}$. 	
    54		When
    55	  the number of variables is clear from context we
    56	  write $\ideg_d$. We denote by $\deg_{d}$ the set of polynomials with
    57	  \emph{total} degree at most $d$.
    58	\end{definition}
    59	
    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. 
    61	
    62	
    63	
    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}

   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

Then

   303	$\{M^{\Pair,\omega}_{\beta_X,\beta_Z} \}$ is projective,
   304	\Cref{eq:lc-11} puts us in

   313	on average over commuting $\omega$. Then for every $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, since the measurements $\{M^{\tvar,x}_a\}$ are projective we get that
   314	\begin{align}

   320	in~\eqref{eq:lc-12}, and performing the same steps in reverse, we deduce that on average over commuting $\omega$,
   321	\[

   327	\begin{gather}

   364	\subsection{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   365	\label{sec:expanding}
   366	
   367	\paragraph{Expanded state.} We introduce registers $\alice', \alice'', \bob', \bob''$ that are each isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. Define the state \begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   368		\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} = (\ket{\psi})_{\alice \bob} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice' \alice''} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\bob' \bob''}\;,
   369	\end{equation}
   370	where we have added maximally entangled states in registers
   371	$\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$; recall also that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is already implicitly  appended with sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state. 
   372	For the remainder of the Appendix all approximations will be evaluated with respect to this state.
   373	
   374	\paragraph{Expanded observables.} For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$ define the following observable $\hat{W}^r(u)$: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   375		\hat{W}^r(u) = W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))\;,
   376	\end{equation}
   377	where $W^r(u)$ is the observable defined in \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} and $\tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))$ is the generalized Pauli observable (see \Cref{sec:generalized-pauli}) acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. 
   378	
   379	For $a\in \F_q$ define corresponding projections
   380	\[
   381		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a = \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\;.
   382	\]
   383	Note that $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ can be equivalently
   384	written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
   385	identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
   386	$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
   387	\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
   388	  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
   389	    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}
   390	Then we can write $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_a$ as follows:
   391	\begin{align*}
   392	  \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a
   393	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \,
   394	    W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r
   395	    \cdot \ind_m(u)) \\
   396	    &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   397	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   398	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   399	    \sum_{h \in \F_q^n}
   400	    (-1)^{\tr( r( h \cdot \ind_m(u)))} \tau^{W}_{h} \Big) \\
   401	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   402	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   403	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   404	    \sum_{a'' \in \F_q}
   405	    (-1)^{\tr(a'' r)} \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big) \\
   406	  &=	\sum_{a',a'' \in \F_q} \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr((a + a' + a'')r)} \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \\
   407	  &= \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}  \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\;,
   408	\end{align*}
   409	where in the second line we have used \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} on the
   410	first tensor factor and \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj} on the second, and in the third line we
   411	have used \Cref{eq:qld-point-obs-def}.
   412	For a fixed $u\in\F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$ and $b \in \F_2$, define a projection
   413	\begin{equation}
   414		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \sum_{a \in \F_q : \tr(ar) = b}
   415	        \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \label{eq:qld-def-mptur}
   416	\end{equation}
   417	which can be equivalently written as
   418	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
   419	\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \frac{1}{2} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\;.
   420	\end{equation}
   421	
   422	The registers that the operators $\hat{W}^r(u)$,
   423	$\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, and $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b$ act on
   424	depend on context. For example if $W^r(u)$ is viewed as an operator
   425	acting on register $\alice$, then we will view $\hat{W}^r(u)$ as
   426	acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (with the $\tau^W$ observable
   427	acting on register $\alice'$). We generally indicate via subscripts
   428	which registers the operators act on (for example we will write
   429	$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\alice \alice'}$ or $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\bob
   430	  \alice''}$).

   433	
   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.
   461	
   462	\begin{lemma}
   463	\label{lem:qld-comm-cons}
   464		There exists a function $\delta_{\acom}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   465	
   466	
   467	\begin{enumerate}
   468		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $r \in \F_q$ and $u\in \F_q^m$, we have 
   469		\[
   470			(\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\eps (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\bob \alice''}\,.
   471			\]
   472		\item (\textbf{Approximate commutation}) On average over
   473	          uniformly random $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$,
   474	          we have 
   475		\[
   476			(\hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b}
   477	                \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'})_{\alice
   478	                  \alice'} \approx_{\delta_{\acom}}
   479	                (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'}
   480	                \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b})_{\alice
   481	                  \alice'} \;.
   482		\]
   483	      \end{enumerate}
   484	      Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   485	      also hold.
   486	\end{lemma}
   487	
   488	\begin{proof}
   489	Item 1, the self-consistency of $\{\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$, follows from the fact that the original points measurements $\{ M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$ are approximately self-consistent between registers $\alice$ and $\bob$ in $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ (item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}), the Pauli projections $\{\tau^W_a(\ind_m(u))\}$ are perfectly self-consistent between registers $\alice'$ and $\alice''$, and~\Cref{fact:data-processing}. 
   490		
   491		We now establish the approximate commutation relations. On average over uniformly random $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have
   492		\begin{align*}
   493		&\hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b} \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'}  \label{eq:qld-m-x-m-z} \\

   501	         & \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \\

   506	                                             \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt))
   507	                                             \tau^Z(r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)) \\

   518	        $\tau^X(r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt))$ observables. This shows

   523	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}
   524	There exists a function $\delta_{\Line}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   525		For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and lines $\line$ there exists a projective measurement $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}_{f \in \deg_{md}(\line)}$, acting on registers $\alice\alice'$ or $\bob\alice''$, such that:
   526		\begin{enumerate}
   527			\item  (\textbf{Self-consistency})\label{enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons}  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$, on average over a uniformly random  pair $(\line, u)$
   528	                drawn from the line-point distribution
   529	                (\Cref{def:line-point-dist}),
   530			\[
   531				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   532			\]
   533			
   534			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements I}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}
   535			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   536	                drawn from the line-point distribution, 
   537			\[
   538				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   539			\]		
   540			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements II}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   541			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   542	                drawn from the line-point distribution,
   543			\[
   544				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line}  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   545			\]
   546	              \end{enumerate}
   547	                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   548	      also hold.
   549	\end{lemma}

   552		Define the operator
   553		\[
   554			\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f = \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' = f}} M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''}\;,
   555		\]
   556		where the Pauli operator $\tau^{W,\line}_{f''}$ acting on register $\alice'$ is obtained by measuring all $\nqubits$ qudits in the basis $W$ to obtain an outcome $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and then returning the restriction $f''$ of $g_h: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ to the line $\line$. Here, $g_h$ is the degree-$d$ low-degree extension of $h$ defined in~\eqref{eq:ld-encoding}.

   560	\Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, the consistency with the points measurements, follows because on average over $(\line,u)$ drawn from the line-point distribution we have

   563		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   564	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   565	  \alice'} \\
   566	        &= \sum_{\substack{f', f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line): \\ f' + f'' =
   567	  f}} ((M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W, \line}_{f''})
   568	  \cdot (M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = f'(u)]} )_{\alice
   569	  \alice'} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-1} \\
   570		&\approx_\eps \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\
   571	  f' + f'' = f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes
   572	  \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes
   573	  (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)})_{\bob
   574	  \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} \\
   575	  	&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   576	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   577	  \alice'} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)} \otimes
   578	  \tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-3} \\
   579		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   580	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   581	  \alice'} \otimes \Big (\sum_{\substack{a', a'' : \\ a' + a'' = f'(u)
   582	  + f''(u)}}  M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'} \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big
   583	  )_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-4} \\
   584		&= (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes

   588	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f}\}$. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} follows from the consistency between the line
   589	and point measurements (\Cref{enu:qld-ld} in
   590	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}) together with
   591	\Cref{fact:add-a-proj2}. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-3}
   592	follows from the exact consistency between the $\{ \tau^{W,\line}_{f''} \}$ and $\{

   595	= f''(u)$ . This establishes \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, with
   596	approximation error $\eps$.

   598	To show \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} we would like to first

   607	  \line}_f )^2 \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{f(u)})^2 \ket{\hat{\psi}}

   609	                 &= \E_{\omega} \sum_{f} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),

   615	                 &=\E_{\omega} \sum_{a}  \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   616	                   \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]}  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   617	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}},

   620	measurements $\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_f\}$ and
   621	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}\}$.
   622	Thus, we have deduced that

   631	&= \sum_a \Big((\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   632	                                                               a]})_{\alice
   633	                                                               \alice'}
   634	                                                               \ot
   635	                                                               I_{\bob
   636	                                                               \alice''}-(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\Big) \notag\\
   637	&\qquad\qquad + \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.\label{eq:com-1a}
   638	\end{align}
   639	For projective sub-measurements $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_i\}$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$,
   640	\begin{align*}
   641	\sum_i \bra{\varphi}\big(A_i-B_i\big)\ket{\varphi} &= \sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i(A_i-B_i)\ket{\varphi} + \sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)B_i\ket{\varphi}\\
   642	&\leq \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i^2\ket{\varphi} \Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2} \\
   643	&\qquad\qquad+ \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}B_i^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\\
   644	&\leq 2\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\;.
   645	\end{align*}
   646	Applying this fact to the projective sub-measurements $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'}\}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:com-1a} and using~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-1} gives
   647	\begin{equation}
   648	\label{eq:qld-comm-line-2}
   649		\Id \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   650	      \end{equation}
   651	      To go from~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} to \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} of the lemma we use another fact about
   652	      projective measurements. For families of projective measurements $\{A^x_i\}$
   653	      and $\{B^x_i\}$ acting on separate registers of a bipartite state
   654	      $\ket{\phi}$, suppose $I \approx_{\delta} \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i$. Then
   655	      \begin{align*}
   656	        \delta &\geq \E_{x} \Big\| \Big(\Id - \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i\Big) \ket{\phi}\Big\|^2  \\
   657	               &= \E_{x} \Big(1 + \bra{\phi} \Big(\sum_i A^x_i \ot
   658	                 B^x_i\Big)^2 \ket{\phi} - 2 \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i
   659	                 \ket{\phi} \Big) \\
   660	               &= 1 - \E_{x} \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i \ket{\phi}\;,

   663	      the third line, to remove the square. Thus

   671	        u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} gives

   673		(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}.

   676	      this yields the conclusion of \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   677	      of the lemma.
   678	\end{proof}

    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   110	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   111	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   112	
   113	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   114	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   115	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   116	  fun i =>
   117	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   118	
   119	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   120	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   121	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   122	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   123	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   124	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   125	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   126	
   127	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   128	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   129	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   130	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   131	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   132	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   133	  classical
   134	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   135	    some (Classical.choose h)
   136	  else none
   137	
   138	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   139	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   140	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   141	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   142	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   143	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   144	
   145	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   147	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   151	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   152	      intro j hj
   153	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   154	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   155	
   156	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   157	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   158	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   159	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   160	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   161	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   162	
   163	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   171	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   172	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   173	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   174	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   175	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   176	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   177	
   178	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   179	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   180	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   181	  sorry
   182	
   183	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   184	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   185	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   186	  sorry
   187	
   188	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   189	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   190	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   191	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   192	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   193	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   194	
   195	end

    24	/--

    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)

   548		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:anticommuting-tuple, def:pauli-question-distribution, def:pauli-win-predicate, def:line-point-dist, def:consistency, def:povm-distance, def:ms-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:low-degree-encoding, def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
   549		Assume that $\mathcal{S}$ succeeds in $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$
   550		with probability at least $1 - \eps$, for some $\eps \geq 0$. Then the
   551		following hold, with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$ of the strategy
   552		under analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the
   553		convention following it).
   554		\begin{enumerate}
   555			\item \label{enu:qld-cons} (\textbf{Consistency check}) On average
   556			over $(\mathsf{t},x)$ sampled from the question distribution of
   557			$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$
   558			(Definition~\ref{def:pauli-question-distribution}), we have
   559			$M^{\mathsf{t},x}_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \simeq_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{\mathsf{t},x}_a$.
   560			\item \label{enu:qld-ld} (\textbf{Low-degree check}) For all
   561			$W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $(\ell,u)$ drawn from the
   562			line-point distribution (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}), we
   563			have
   564			% The source states this item with answer summation over F_q only,
   565			% implicitly reading the evaluation classes of the line measurement
   566			% as a complete measurement; see the paragraph after the item list
   567			% and the remark rem:qld-win-implications-typos.
   568			$M^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \simeq_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$,
   569			where the answer summation is over the completed outcome set
   570			$a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$ described after the item list.
   571			\item \label{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} (\textbf{Pauli basis
   572			consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over
   573			uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$, we have
   574			$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \simeq_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]}$,
   575			where
   576			$M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{M} \colon g_h(u)=a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$
   577			and $g_h$ is the low-degree encoding of $h$
   578			(see Definition~\ref{def:low-degree-encoding}).
   579			\item \label{enu:qld-comm} (\textbf{Commutation check}) For all
   580			$W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting
   581			$\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ (that is, over a uniformly random
   582			$\omega$ conditioned on being commuting), we have
   583			$M^{(\mathrm{Pair},W),\omega}_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \simeq_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{\mathrm{Pair},\omega}_{[\beta_W=a]}$,
   584			where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$.
   585			\item \label{enu:qld-comm-cons} (\textbf{Commutation consistency
   586			check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting
   587			$\omega$, we have
   588			$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_W)=a]} \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \simeq_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{(\mathrm{Pair},W),\omega}_a$,
   589			where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$.
   590			\item \label{enu:qld-ms} (\textbf{Magic square check}) For any
   591			anticommuting $\omega$, let $\Lambda_\omega$ be the value of the
   592			strategy
   593			$\big( \ket{\psi}, \{M^{\mathrm{Constraint}_i,\omega}_{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3}\} \cup \{M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega}_a\} \big)$
   594			in the Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$
   595			(Definition~\ref{def:ms-game}). Then
   596			$\E_\omega \Lambda_\omega = 1 - O(\eps)$, where the expectation is
   597			over a uniformly random $\omega$ conditioned on being
   598			anticommuting.
   599			\item \label{enu:qld-ms-cons} (\textbf{Magic square consistency
   600			check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over anticommuting
   601			$\omega$,
   602			\begin{gather*}
   603				M^{(\mathrm{Point},X),u_X}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_X)=a]} \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \,\simeq_\eps\, \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_1,\omega}_a\,,\\
   604				M^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),u_Z}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_Z)=a]} \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \,\simeq_\eps\, \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_5,\omega}_a\,,
   605			\end{gather*}
   606			where the answer summations are over $\F_2$.
   607		\end{enumerate}
   608		Here
   609		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r)=a]} = \sum_{a' \in \F_q \colon \tr(a'r)=a} M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{a'}$
   610		for $a \in \F_2$; in item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} the two families are the

   614		Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}, whose class
   615		$M^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ carries the
   616		line answers with no evaluation at $u$ and is nonzero only for a
   617		zero-direction line, where the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form
   618		only a sub-measurement; on the right, the point measurement completed
   619		by the zero operator $M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot} = 0$; the answer
   620		to a question of type $\mathrm{Pair}$ is a
   621		pair $(\beta_X,\beta_Z) \in \F_2 \times \F_2$, and
   622		$M^{\mathrm{Pair},\omega}_{[\beta_W=a]}$ denotes its coarse-graining
   623		onto the $W$-component. Furthermore, all of the approximations above
   624		also hold with $\approx_\eps$ in place of $\simeq_\eps$, and with the
   625		tensor factors interchanged.
   626	\end{lemma}
   627	\begin{proof}
   628		\uses{fact:omega-anticomm-prob, fact:agreement, def:admissible, def:pauli-question-distribution, def:pauli-win-predicate, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ideg-deg-polynomials, def:consistency}
   629		The question types are sampled according to the type graph of the Pauli
   630		basis test (Definition~\ref{def:pauli-question-distribution}), which has
   631		constant size, so each subtest of the win predicate
   632		(Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}) is executed with probability
   633		bounded below by a universal constant.
   634		Items~\ref{enu:qld-cons},~\ref{enu:qld-ld}
   635		and~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} then follow directly from the
   636		corresponding subtests and the assumption that $\mathcal{S}$ succeeds
   637		with probability at least $1-\eps$, where item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} follows
   638		from the consistency subtest of the low individual degree game executed
   639		inside the Pauli basis test. In more detail for item~\ref{enu:qld-ld}:
   640		the disagreement mass of the two completed families is rejection mass
   641		of the line-versus-point clauses
   642		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}, invoked by the low-degree
   643		check of Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}). An outcome pair
   644		$(a,b)$ with $a \neq b$ in $\F_q$ is a line answer evaluating at $u$
   645		to $a$ against the point answer $b$, which the clause rejects; a pair
   646		$(\bot,b)$ is a line answer with no evaluation at $u$, which the
   647		universally quantified clause rejects against every point answer $b$
   648		(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction} and
   649		Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}); and the pairs $(a,\bot)$
   650		contribute no mass, since the class
   651		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot}$ is the zero operator. The subtests underlying
   652		items~\ref{enu:qld-comm} and~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} accept vacuously
   653		unless the sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting, and those underlying
   654		items~\ref{enu:qld-ms} and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} accept vacuously
   655		unless $\omega$ is anticommuting. Since the parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   656		is admissible (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), $m$ divides $q$, so
   657		$1 \leq m \leq q$, and Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} shows that
   658		a uniformly sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting with probability at
   659		least $\frac12$ and anticommuting with probability at least $2^{-4}$.
   660		Conditioning on either event therefore increases the failure
   661		probability of the corresponding subtest by a factor of at most $2^4$,
   662		and items~\ref{enu:qld-comm},~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons}
   663		and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} follow from the corresponding subtests.
   664		Item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} follows in the same way, because the Magic Square
   665		check is executed with constant probability over the choice of a pair
   666		of questions and the anticommuting event has probability at least
   667		$2^{-4}$. Finally, that all approximations
   668		also hold with $\approx_\eps$ in place of $\simeq_\eps$ is immediate
   669		from Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.
   670	\end{proof}

   795	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   796	\label{sec:expanding}
   797	
   798	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   799	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   800	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   801	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   802	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for
   803	every tuple $\omega$.

    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}.

    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

   134	The following lemma shows that POVMs that are approximately projective (in the sense of being self-consistent) are close to exact projective measurements. The lemma first appears in~\cite{KV11}; for a self-contained proof, see~\cite{ML20}.

   136	\begin{lemma}[Orthonormalization lemma]\label{lem:ortho}
   137	Let $0\leq \delta\leq 1$. There exists a function $\eta_{ortho}(\delta)\,=\, O\big(\delta^{1/4}\big)$ such that the following holds.  Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state on $\mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ where $\mH_\alice,\mH_\bob$ are finite dimensional. Let $\{Q_a\}$ and $\{R_a\}$ be POVM on $\mH_\alice$ and $\mH_\bob$ respectively such that 
   138	\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-cond} 
   139	Q_a \abc R_a \,.
   140	\end{equation}
   141	Then there exists a projective measurement $\{P_a\}$ such that
   142	\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-ccl}
   143	  P_a \otimes \Id_\bob \,\approx_{\eta_{ortho}} Q_a \otimes \Id_\bob \;.
   144	\end{equation}
   145	\end{lemma}

   197	\begin{lemma}
   198	\label{lem:qld-win-implications}
   199	Assume that $\strategy$ succeeds in $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ with probability at least $1-\eps$, for some $\eps\geq 0$. Then the following hold: 
   200		\begin{enumerate}
   201			\item \label{enu:qld-cons} (\textbf{Consistency check}) On average over $(\tvar,x)$ sampled from the question distribution of $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$, we have that $M^{\tvar,x}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\tvar,x}_a$.
   202			\item \label{enu:qld-ld} (\textbf{Low-degree check})
   203	                  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $(\line,u)$
   204	                  drawn from the line-point distribution (see
   205	                  Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}), we
   206	                  have $M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_q$. 
   207			
   208		\item \label{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} (\textbf{Pauli basis consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]}$ where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$ and $g_h$ is the low-degree encoding of $h$. 
   209		
   210			\item \label{enu:qld-comm} (\textbf{Commutation check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}$, where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$.
   211			\item \label{enu:qld-comm-cons} (\textbf{Commutation consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_{a}$, where the answer summation is over $a\in \F_2$.
   212			
   213			\item\label{enu:qld-ms} (\textbf{Magic square check}) For any anticommuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ let $\Lambda_\omega$ be the value of the strategy $\Big (\ket{\psi}, \{M^{\Constraint_i,\omega}_{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3}\} \cup \{M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_a \} \Big )$ in the game $\game^\ms$. Then 
   214			\[
   215				\E_{\omega \, : \, \tr((r_\xpt \cdot
   216	                          u_\xpt) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot u_\zpt)) \neq 0} \Lambda_\omega = 1 - O(\eps)\;.
   217			\]
   218	
   219		\item \label{enu:qld-ms-cons} (\textbf{Magic square consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over anticommuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$,
   220		\begin{gather}
   221			M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_{a} \;,\\
   222			M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}_{a}\;,

   226		\end{enumerate}
   227		Furthermore, all of the approximations above hold with ``$\approx_\eps$'' instead of ``$\simeq_\eps$'', and they also hold with the tensor factors interchanged.

   230	\begin{proof}
   231		Since the question types are sampled according to the type graph $G^\Pauli$ of
   232	  finite size in \cref{fig:type-graph-pauli} in the game
   233	  $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$, the probability of any of the subtests of
   234	  $\decider^\pauli_\qldparams$ (described in \cref{fig:decider_pauli})
   235	  being executed is at least some universal constant.
   236	  Thus the consistency conditions expressed in Items
   237	  \ref{enu:qld-cons},~\ref{enu:qld-ld},~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} of the
   238	  lemma follow directly from the corresponding tests in
   239	  \cref{fig:decider_pauli} (where \Cref{enu:qld-ld} follows from the
   240	  consistency test that is a subtest of $\decider^\ld_\ldparams$) and the fact

   243					
   244	  For the remaining items, recall that by Fact~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   245	  the probability that a tuple $\omega=(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled as

   247	  or $\Variable_j$ is commuting is at least $(1 - 3md/q) \cdot (1/2)$, which is

   265	\end{proof}

   290	where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$. Equation~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-consistency} follows directly from~\Cref{lem:povm-to-obs}. 
   291	
   292	We now establish~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}. We have that on average over {commuting} $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ each of the approximate consistency relations hold, for any $W\in\{X,Z\}$:
   293	\begin{align*}
   294		&& M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W)=a]} \otimes \Id_\bob &\simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_a && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications})}\\
   295		&& &\simeq_\eps M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-comm})} \\
   296		&& &\simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}\;. && \text{(Item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} and Fact~\ref{fact:data-processing})}
   297	\end{align*}
   298	Fact~\ref{fact:agreement} then implies that on average over commuting $\omega$, 
   299	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-11}
   300		M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W)=a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}\;.
   301	\end{equation}
   302	Since
   303	$\{M^{\Pair,\omega}_{\beta_X,\beta_Z} \}$ is projective,
   304	\Cref{eq:lc-11} puts us in
   305	a position to apply Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}, setting
   306	$A^{x}_{a,b} = M^{(\Point, X), u_X}_{[\tr(\cdot r_X) = b]}$,
   307	$C^{x}_{a,c} = M^{(\Point, Z), u_Z}_{[\tr(\cdot r_Z) = c]}$, and
   308	$B^{x}_{a,b,c} = M^{\Pair, \omega}_{b,c}$. It follows that
   309	\begin{equation}
   310	\label{eq:qld-obs-comm}
   311		 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=b]} M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=c]} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps  M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=c]} M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=b]}  \otimes \Id_\bob
   312	\end{equation}
   313	on average over commuting $\omega$. Then for every $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, since the measurements $\{M^{\tvar,x}_a\}$ are projective we get that
   314	\begin{align}
   315		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) &= \Big ( \Id - 2 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} \Big ) \Big ( \Id - 2 M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]}  \Big ) \notag\\
   316		&= I - 2 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} - 2 M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]} + 4 M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt)=1]} M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt)=1]}\;.\label{eq:lc-12}
   317	\end{align}
   318	Applying~\eqref{eq:qld-obs-comm} with $b = c = 1$ to commute the
   319	measurement operators in the the fourth term
   320	in~\eqref{eq:lc-12}, and performing the same steps in reverse, we deduce that on average over commuting $\omega$,
   321	\[
   322		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \approx_\eps  Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt).
   323	\]
   324	This shows the ``commuting'' part of~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}.
   325	
   326	Now we consider the case that $\omega$ is anticommuting. Item~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}, combined with \Cref{lem:povm-to-obs}, implies that the following two approximations hold on average over anticommuting $\omega$:
   327	\begin{gather}
   328		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} \;,\label{eq:lc-11a}\\
   329		Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}\;,\label{eq:lc-11b}
   330	\end{gather}
   331	where for $j\in\{1,5\}$, $M^{\Variable_j,\omega} = M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_0-M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_1$.
   332	
   333	For all anticommuting $\omega$, let $\eps_\omega = 1 -
   334	\Lambda_\omega$, where $\Lambda_\omega$ is defined in
   335	item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}. From
   336	item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} we get
   337	that $\E_{\omega \text{ anticomm.}} \eps_\omega \leq
   338	O(\eps)$. For each anticommuting $\omega$,
   339	Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity} implies that
   340	\[ \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   341	  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   342	  M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;. \]
   343	Thus, averaging over anticommuting $\omega$, and applying Jensen's
   344	inequality to the definition of $\approx_{\eps}$, we obtain the same
   345	anticommutation relation with error $ \E_{\omega \text{anticomm.}}
   346	\eps_{\omega}^{1/2} \leq (\E_{\omega \text{anticomm.}}
   347	\eps_\omega)^{1/2} = O(\eps^{1/2})$. In summary, on average over anticommuting $\omega$, 
   348	\begin{equation}
   349	\label{eq:qld-implication-ms-anticomm}
   350	\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} -\Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;.
   351	\end{equation}
   352	Using \ref{fact:add-a-proj} twice we get from~\eqref{eq:lc-11a} and~\eqref{eq:lc-11b} that on average over anticommuting $\omega$,
   353	\begin{gather}
   354		X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega}  M^{\Variable_5,\omega}\;, \\
   355		Z^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) X^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}  M^{\Variable_1,\omega}\;.
   356	\end{gather}
   357	Using~\eqref{eq:qld-implication-ms-anticomm} we get that on average over anticommuting $\omega$, we have
   358	\[
   359	X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt)X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)  \otimes \Id_\bob\;.
   360	\]
   361	This shows the ``anticommuting'' part of~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}.
   362	\end{proof}
